_why: WSG-4. A named-test kill was scored on `that test failed`, which still covers two events wearing one `1 failed`: the guard's assertion bit, or the mutant CRASHED before the property was reached. The module docstring named two measured cases (an unbound-variable crash tripping `assert r.returncode == 0`, and a 60-second TimeoutExpired) and presented the gap as unfixable. Tier 1 -- a mutated file that did not PARSE -- is now refused, because a file that did not parse cannot have exercised a guard. Tier 2 -- every other exception -- is annotated and counted, never refused, because a mutation that strips a None-check makes the code raise and the test asserting the graceful message then fails, where the crash IS the property violation. These mutations cover BOTH directions: the permissive one (the classifier never fires, so crash kills read as clean) and the over-firing ones (an ordinary assertion kill misreported as a crash). Each mutation carries its own `test` key.

mutations.name: the-classifier-never-fires
mutations._mechanism: The permissive direction, and the state before this change: every crash kill reads as an ordinary assertion kill, `crash_kills` stays 0 forever, and the token line says the same thing whether the guard bit or the mutant crashed. Indistinguishable from a suite with no crash kills in it.
mutations.find:
if target in files:
            return exception
mutations.replace:
if target in files:
            return None

mutations.name: the-attribution-check-is-dropped
mutations._mechanism: The over-firing direction. Any traceback anywhere in the run's output is credited to the mutated file, so an ordinary assertion failure -- whose pytest footer attributes it to the TEST file -- is reported as `(crash: AssertionError in <target>)` and inflates crash_kills. A gate reading the count would then see crash kills everywhere and the number would mean nothing.

mutations.name: the-structured-scan-becomes-a-bare-word-search
mutations._mechanism: The loose design this one was written against, expressed as a mutation. A bare `Traceback` search plus the basename anywhere in the output fires on the ECHOED SOURCE of any test whose subject is a crash -- this suite has one (`test_a_non_utf8_log_does_not_crash` asserts `"Traceback" not in stderr`) -- so the classification would be loudest exactly on the tests written about crashes.
mutations.replace:
target = Path(mutated_file).name
    if "Traceback" in output and target in output:
        return "RuntimeError"
    return None

mutations.name: tier-1-is-demoted-to-tier-2
mutations._mechanism: A file that did not parse is counted as a kill instead of refused. That is the whole defect back again in its most confident form: the mutation broke the file, the named test failed, and ALL_CAUGHT is printed -- a green mutation report over a guard that was never executed.

mutations.name: the-count-never-reaches-the-token-line
mutations._mechanism: The annotation stays on the detail line and the summary line reads crash_kills=0. Anything that scores a run by its token -- which is the contract, since callers read the token and never $? -- goes blind while the per-mutation detail still looks right to a human reading the whole report.

mutations.name: the-counter-is-never-incremented
mutations._mechanism: Separable from the token-line mutation above: here the mechanism line is annotated correctly and only the COUNT is lost, so a report that reads right per-mutation still totals to zero.

mutations.name: the-pytest-marker-swallows-exception-names-beginning-with-e
mutations._mechanism: `^\s*E\s+` with the whitespace made optional strips the `E` from `EOFError`, `Exception` and `EnvironmentError` on an UNMARKED line -- which is what pytest's captured-stdout sections carry -- so those crashes classify as nothing and read as ordinary assertion kills. Silent, and only for some exception types.

mutations.name: dotted-exception-names-stop-matching
mutations._mechanism: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` is a real terminal line in this suite's subprocess tests. A bare `\w+` misses every qualified name, so an entire family of crashes reads as clean assertion kills.

mutations.name: the-direct-import-shape-loses-its-only-attribution
mutations._mechanism: pytest prints no `Traceback` header and no `File "..."` frames of its own, so the footer line is the ONLY thing tying a direct-import crash to the mutated file. Drop it and every directly-imported module's crash kills classify as assertions.

mutations.name: the-headerless-compile-error-is-never-seen
mutations._mechanism: CPython reports a compile-time SyntaxError with NO `Traceback` header, and when the child's stderr is embedded in an assertion message the `File "..."` arrives on the SAME line as `AssertionError:`. Stop scanning the rest of that line and tier 1 -- the only tier that refuses -- becomes unreachable through the shape it exists for.

mutations.name: frames-leak-across-reports
mutations._mechanism: Captured output is routinely truncated mid-traceback. Without the reset at each header the surviving frames ride forward, and the next exception is attributed to a file that had nothing to do with it -- a false crash attribution that looks exactly like a true one.
